title: Hierarchy of time scales in kinetically constrained models via stochastic-generator expansion
authors: Vanja Marić, Juan P. Garrahan, Lenart Zadnik
abstract: We revisit the hierarchy of relaxation time scales in stochastic kinetically constrained models (KCMs) obeying detailed balance, using an expansion method developed recently for their quantum counterparts. In the classical setting, we expand the stochastic generator in the low-temperature equilibrium concentration of excitations. As in quantum KCMs, successive truncations of the expansion reveal a nested hierarchy of metastable configurations that remain frozen on progressively longer time scales. Applying the method to the high-to-low temperature quench in the classical one-dimensional East and Fredrickson-Andersen models, we recover the known hierarchy of metastable plateaus and the associated perturbative time scales. We find that the hierarchical time scales are related to the smallest domain lengths. Our results show that the method developed for quantum kinetically constrained models can be used to provide a systematic description of slow relaxation in their classical counterparts as well.
summary: This paper develops and applies a stochastic-generator expansion method to analyze the slow relaxation dynamics in kinetically constrained models (KCMs). By expanding the system's dynamics in terms of the low-temperature excitation concentration, the authors systematically predict the nested hierarchy of metastable states. This work provides a unified theoretical framework connecting quantum and classical descriptions of glassy dynamics.
main_problem: The paper revisits the complex hierarchy of relaxation time scales observed in stochastic kinetically constrained models (KCMs). It aims to provide a systematic theoretical description of this slow relaxation process.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that an expansion method, adapted from quantum KCMs, successfully recovers the known nested hierarchy of metastable plateaus in classical KCMs like the East and Fredrickson-Andersen models.
method: The core method is a low-temperature expansion of the stochastic generator in powers of the equilibrium concentration of excitations. This systematic expansion allows for the identification of successive metastable states.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Kinetically Constrained Models (KCMs), specifically applied to the one-dimensional East and Fredrickson-Andersen (FA) models. The dynamics are governed by a master equation defined by a stochastic generator.
key_observables: Relaxation time scales, nested hierarchy of metastable configurations, and the decay of correlation functions following a quench.
important_parameters: The equilibrium concentration of excitations ($c$) serves as the small expansion parameter. The quench process (high-to-low temperature) is crucial for observing the hierarchy.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system obeys detailed balance, allowing for the symmetrization of the stochastic generator. The method relies on the existence of a small parameter ($c$) governing the hopping rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hierarchical relaxation of energy in the East model and show the time evolution of the effective number of configurations for both the East and FA models after a quench.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the mathematical framework using the stochastic-generator expansion, then applying this method to the classical East and FA models, and finally demonstrating that the resulting time scales systematically reproduce known results for glassy relaxation.
why_interesting: Although focused on classical models, the successful adaptation of a quantum-derived expansion technique to describe slow relaxation in classical stochastic systems provides a powerful, generalizable theoretical tool for understanding glassy dynamics in many-body systems.
